mai.title: औपनिवेशिक ज्ञान की करैत अछि?
mai.summary: औपनिवेशिक ज्ञानक मूल कार्य केवल उपनिवेशित समाजक “चित्र” बनाब नहि छल; ई समाजकेँ राज्य-पठनीय, तुलनीय, करयोग्य, (map)योग्य, कानूनयोग्य आ (classificatory object) बनाबयमे भाग लेलक। एहि प्रक्रियामे वास्तविक ज्ञान, गलत धारणा, (administrative convenience), (scholarly curiosity) आ राजनीतिक शक्ति एक-दोसरासँ गुंथल रहल। एहि कारण द्वैध निर्णय—“सभ औपनिवेशिक ज्ञान झूठ” अथवा “(science) राजनीति सँ स्वतंत्र”—दुनू असफल।

en.title: What Does Colonial Knowledge Do?
en.summary: The basic work of colonial knowledge was not merely to create a “picture” of colonised society; it helped make society state-legible, comparable, taxable, mappable, legally manageable and classifiable. In this process, real knowledge, false assumptions, administrative convenience, scholarly curiosity and political power remained intertwined. For this reason, both binary judgements—“all colonial knowledge is false” and “science is independent of politics”—fail.

mai.title: एडवर्ड सईद: प्राच्यवाद (Orientalism)
mai.summary: (Orientalism)क स्थायी महत्त्व एहि प्रश्नमे अछि जे ज्ञान केना (authority) पबैत अछि। कोनो (society) सम्बन्धी कथन केवल (sentence) नहि; (archive), (institution), (audience), (geopolitical relation) आ (repeated representation)क इतिहास ओकर प्रभाव निर्धारित करैत अछि। सईदक आलोचना बाहरी अध्ययन निषिद्ध नहि करैत; ओ अध्ययनक (asymmetry visible) करैत अछि।

en.title: Edward Said: Orientalism
en.summary: The enduring importance of Orientalism lies in the question of how knowledge acquires authority. A statement about a society is never only a sentence; the histories of archives, institutions, audiences, geopolitical relations and repeated representations determine its effects. Said’s critique does not prohibit outsiders from studying other societies; it makes the asymmetry of such study visible.

mai.title: गायत्री स्पिवाक: अधीनस्थ बोलि सकैत अछि?
mai.summary: (Spivak)क स्थायी योगदान ई नहि जे ओ (oppressed) लोकक (agency) अस्वीकार करैत छथि, वरन् ई जे (agency)क (social intelligibility) केँ (philosophical problem) बनबैत छथि। वाणी, (representation), (archive), (gender) आ (institution)क बीच संबंध बिना “(voice)”क नारा अधूरा अछि। अधीनस्थता (identity) नहि, (structural relation) अछि।

en.title: Gayatri Spivak: Can the Subaltern Speak?
en.summary: Spivak’s enduring contribution is not that she denies the agency of oppressed people, but that she makes the social intelligibility of agency a philosophical problem. Without attending to the relations among speech, representation, archive, gender and institution, the slogan of “voice” remains incomplete. Subalternity is not an identity but a structural relation.

mai.title: होमी भाभा: संकरता आ औपनिवेशिक अन्तराल
mai.summary: भाभाक मुख्य योगदान औपनिवेशिक सत्ता केँ (monolithic machine) नहि, (contradictory authority) रूपमे पढ़ब अछि। (universal norm)क दावा आ (racial/cultural hierarchy)क (practice) बीच तनाव (ambivalence) उत्पन्न करैत अछि। (stereotype fixed truth)क मुखौटा लगबैत अछि, मुदा ओकर (compulsive repetition instability) प्रकट करैत अछि।

en.title: Homi Bhabha: Hybridity and the Colonial Interstice
en.summary: Bhabha’s principal contribution is to read colonial power not as a monolithic machine but as contradictory authority. The tension between claims to universal norms and practices of racial or cultural hierarchy produces ambivalence. The stereotype wears the mask of fixed truth, yet its compulsive repetition reveals instability.

mai.title: अधीनस्थ अध्ययन (Subaltern Studies) आ इतिहासक हाशिया
mai.summary: (Subaltern Studies) इतिहास-लेखनमे एक मूल प्रश्न स्थापित कएलक: जनसाधारणक राजनीति केँ (elite initiative)क (derivative) मानब स्वयं (historiographical bias) हो सकैत अछि। रणजीत गुहाक “(autonomous domain)”क सर्वोत्तम अर्थ पूर्ण अलगाव नहि, (anti-reductionism) अछि—(popular politics)क अपन (idiom), (network), (grievance) आ (initiative) जाँचू। (counter-insurgency archive) केँ आलोचनात्मक पढ़नाइ आवश्यक, मुदा (archive)क उल्टा अर्थ स्वतः सत्य नहि।

en.title: Subaltern Studies and the Margins of History
en.summary: Subaltern Studies established a foundational question in historiography: treating popular politics as derivative of elite initiative may itself be a historiographical bias. The strongest meaning of Ranajit Guha’s “autonomous domain” is not complete separation but anti-reductionism—investigate the idioms, networks, grievances, and initiatives of popular politics in their own right. The counter-insurgency archive must be read critically, but its opposite meaning is not automatically true.

mai.title: उत्तर-औपनिवेशिकतासँ औपनिवेशिकता-मुक्त (decolonial) विचार धरि
mai.summary: उत्तर-औपनिवेशिक विचारसँ (decoloniality) धरि संक्रमण (discourse)क प्रश्न छोड़ि (material power)क प्रश्नपर लौटब मात्र नहि; (representation), (world-system), (race), (labour), (being), (gender), (nature) आ (knowledge) केँ एक जटिल (matrix)मे जोड़बाक प्रयास अछि। (Quijano)क (coloniality of power) औपचारिक (colonialism) समाप्ति आ (domination pattern)क (persistence) बीच महत्त्वपूर्ण भेद स्थापित करैत अछि। मुदा ओकर (Latin American genealogy) स्पष्ट राखब अनिवार्य।

en.title: From Postcoloniality to Decolonial Thought
en.summary: The transition from postcolonial thought to decoloniality is not merely a move away from discourse back to material power; it is an attempt to connect representation, world-system, race, labour, being, gender, nature and knowledge within a complex matrix. Quijano’s coloniality of power establishes an important distinction between the formal end of colonialism and the persistence of patterns of domination. Yet its Latin American genealogy must remain explicit.

mai.title: भारतीय दर्शनक औपनिवेशिक वर्गीकरण
mai.summary: भारतीय दर्शनक औपनिवेशिक वर्गीकरणक इतिहास न (total invention)क कथा अछि, न (neutral discovery)क। (precolonial taxonomies), (colonial institutions) आ (modern Indian reappropriation)क त्रिस्तरीय (interaction) आधुनिक (canon) बनौलक। “(six systems),” “(Hinduism),” “(Indian philosophy),” “(orthodox/heterodox),” “(mysticism)” आदि (labels) उपयोगी हो सकैत छथि, मुदा हुनकर (historical scope), (translation loss) आ (institutional genealogy) स्पष्ट राखब आवश्यक।

en.title: Colonial Classification of Indian Philosophy
en.summary: The history of the colonial classification of Indian philosophy is neither a story of total invention nor one of neutral discovery. The three-level interaction of precolonial taxonomies, colonial institutions, and modern Indian reappropriation shaped the modern canon. Labels such as “six systems,” “Hinduism,” “Indian philosophy,” “orthodox/heterodox,” and “mysticism” can be useful, but their historical scope, translation losses, and institutional genealogies must remain explicit.

mai.title: मिथिला: साम्राज्य, राष्ट्र आ क्षेत्रक बीच
mai.summary: (Mithila) केँ साम्राज्य, राष्ट्र आ क्षेत्रक बीच पढ़ला पर स्पष्ट होइत अछि जे (region neither eternal essence nor arbitrary fiction)। ई दीर्घ (historical relations), (memory), (language), (institution), (ecology) आ (political claim)क परिवर्तनीय संरचना अछि। पूर्व-औपनिवेशिक नाम/स्मृति (modern exact boundary)क स्वतः प्रमाण नहि; (colonial administration regional reality) शून्य सँ बनौलक सेहो नहि।

en.title: Mithila: Between Empire, Nation and Region
en.summary: Reading Mithila between empire, nation and region makes clear that the region is neither an eternal essence nor an arbitrary fiction. It is a changing structure of long historical relations, memory, language, institutions, ecology and political claims. Pre-colonial names and memories are not automatic proof of modern exact boundaries; nor did colonial administration create regional reality from nothing.
